title: Moving into competitions
audience: Brand new junior golfers and their parents or guardians.

pages.markdown:
# Your first competition

Taking part in your first golf competition is an exciting step. It’s normal to feel a mix of nerves and excitement, both for juniors and their families. This learning pack will help you know what to expect when you enter a golf competition for the first time.

You don’t need to be an expert or have expensive equipment—just a little preparation and a positive attitude will help you have fun and do your best. Friendly club staff and experienced junior golfers are always on hand to help, and everyone was a beginner once.

You’ll learn about what to do before your round, how competitions are run, what it’s like during a round, and the important steps after your round finishes. You’ll also find tips for parents so everyone can enjoy the day together. Every competition is a chance to enjoy golf, make friends, and learn new things.

pages.markdown:
# Before you start

Before you arrive at your competition, there are a few simple things to do. Make sure you have your basic golf equipment: a couple of clubs (like a putter and an iron), a ball or two, tees, and comfortable clothes suitable for the weather. Trainers are often fine, and you don’t need to buy special shoes at first.

It’s a good idea to check the start time, as competitions often run on a fixed schedule. Try to get to the club in good time so you don’t need to rush. If you’re not sure where to go, ask at the clubhouse or look for friendly, welcoming stewards—most clubs are well set up to guide new juniors and parents.

Don’t forget to have a snack and a filled water bottle, plus a hat if it’s sunny. Parents and juniors should know where the toilets are and which holes you will be playing. If you’re not sure about anything, it’s always okay to ask a club coach or organiser. They want you to have a great first experience!

pages.title: During the round
pages.imageAlt: Two juniors playing golf calmly on the course, watched from a distance by supportive adults near a pathway.
pages.imagePrompt: A photorealistic image showing two junior golfers playing on the fairway while two relaxed adults (parents or guardians) observe from a respectful distance along a golf path. The children are smiling and taking their shots, with the golf course visible.
pages.markdown:
# During the round

Once your group is called, you’ll go out onto the course with other juniors. Often, you’ll play in small groups called “matches” or “groups.” One of you will be chosen to keep the score—a simple job just marking the number of shots you each take on each hole.

During play, focus on enjoying your shots rather than worrying about perfect scores. Remember to be respectful of other players: wait quietly while others play their shots and be ready when it’s your turn. If your ball goes somewhere you didn’t expect, don’t worry—everyone has tricky shots sometimes!

Parents and carers are usually welcome to walk along the side of the course, but they should avoid giving advice about how to play golf during the round, as this can be against competition rules. Lots of encouragement is always allowed! Be sure to drink water and stay sun safe.

If you’re unsure about what to do, ask your group or a club helper. It’s all about learning and enjoying the day together.

pages.imageAlt: Juniors and parents gathered by a clubhouse, chatting and smiling after a round of golf.

pages.markdown:
# After the round

When you finish playing, all players in your group meet at the end to check and agree on everyone’s scores. Make sure your scorecard is filled out clearly, with no guessing—if you’re not certain about a hole, ask one of the organisers to help. Hand in your scorecard where you’re told, usually at the club’s reception or a special table.

Often, there’s a short wait while results are checked. This is a great time to have a snack and chat about your round with other juniors and families. Sometimes there are prizes, but the main aim is to have fun, make friends, and learn.

Parents, encourage your junior even if their score isn’t what they hoped for. Every round helps you improve! Remember to say thanks to organisers and volunteers—they work hard to make competitions welcoming and fair for everyone. Enjoy the day and be proud of taking part.

pages.markdown:
# Quick check

Let’s see what you remember! These questions will help you feel ready for your first competition.

questions.question: What should you bring to your first competition?

choices.text: A hat, water bottle, simple clubs, comfortable clothes, and a snack
Expensive new clubs and fancy clothes
Only golf balls
Nothing at all

questions.explanation: You just need basic equipment to get started, plus a snack and hat if it’s sunny.

questions.question: What can parents do while juniors are playing?

choices.text: Give advice on every shot
Stay nearby, offer encouragement, and watch with other parents
Run onto the course to help look for balls
Play shots for their child

questions.explanation: Parents can give encouragement but should not give playing advice or interfere with play.

questions.question: What happens at the end of a round?

choices.text: Players shout and run home straight away
Players check scores together and hand in their scorecard
Only the winner fills in their card
Everyone is sent home without checking anything

questions.explanation: Players should check and agree on the scores, then hand in the scorecard as a group.

questions.question: If you are unsure of a rule or what to do during the competition, what should you do?

choices.text: Guess and hope it’s right
Ask a club organiser, coach, or your group
Do nothing
Leave the course

questions.explanation: It’s always okay to ask for help—organisers want you to learn and enjoy the day!

questions.question: The most important thing about your first competition is to...

choices.text: Win at all costs
Have fun, learn, and make friends
Buy the best equipment
Worry about your score

questions.explanation: The main goal is to have a good time, learn new things, and meet new friends.
